ns2:section.sectionText: Topic: Participatory Art. This class is framed by recent debates about "relational aesthetics" and the efficacy of contemporary political art, particularly art that demands spectator participation. Focusing on the social aspects of participation, we will consider international art practices from the late 1950s until the present that seek to activate the viewer, often through physical engagement. Authors and artists to be considered include: Paulo Freire, Roland Barthes, John Cage, Yoko Ono, Umberto Eco, Guy Debord, Allan Kaprow, Helio Oiticica, Lygia Clark, Joseph Beuys, Andrea Fraser, Nicholas Bourriaud, Claire Bishop, Rirkrit Tiravanija, Jacques Ranciere.
